component.name: Hallucinate
component.summary: Play the music you own, lit by its covers

description.p: Hallucinate is a fast desktop music player for your own files. It looks like nothing else: frosted glass over colours drawn from the album that's playing, a waveform seek bar, and a full-screen Now Playing view with visualizers that move with the music.

ul.li: Instant search across artists, albums and songs, and a command palette (Ctrl+K)
Now Playing with Liquid, Aurora and Nebula visualizers and an optional spinning-record mode
Album pages with liner notes, a colour wall of your covers and a timeline by year
A searchable history of every listen with a year-long heatmap
FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis, Opus, AAC, ALAC, WAV, WavPack, AIFF and more
Gapless playback, crossfade, ReplayGain, a 10-band equalizer and a signal path readout
Radio mode, smart playlists, star ratings, liked songs, playlists and listening statistics
Artist pages, a folder view and weekly, monthly and yearly listening recaps
CUE sheet albums, ReplayGain analysis, headphone correction from AutoEQ and crossfeed
Select many songs at once, undo queue changes, and import your history from other players
A library health check with fixes, a tag editor, cover art lookup and synced lyrics
Optional Last.fm and ListenBrainz scrobbling and Discord Rich Presence
Media keys and desktop controls through MPRIS, a mini player and a tray icon
Live-switchable themes, including Catppuccin, Nord, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, Dracula and pride themes

description.p: The Flatpak can read your Music folder; use the folder picker in Settings to add music stored elsewhere.

screenshot.caption: Now Playing over the Aurora visualizer, in the cover's colours
Home: a random album, your listening heatmap and library facts
An album page with liner notes
Every album cover ordered round the colour wheel
The history of every listen, by day
Radio mode keeps the queue going with similar songs

description.p: Hallucinate now has its own signed Flatpak repository: install it from the website and it updates with your other apps.
Big libraries: tested with a quarter of a million songs. Start-up and rescans are faster, opening albums and the timeline no longer stalls, and memory use is a third lower.
The timeline shows two rows of each year, with "Show all" for the rest.

Safety and stability: song tags and lyrics can no longer make the interface go online, the library database is backed up daily and restored automatically if it's ever damaged, a slow memory leak is fixed and the caches stay a sensible size.
Right-click albums, or select several, to play, queue, add to playlists, remove from the library or move to the trash.
Finding covers online copes with the cover servers failing an image.
Searching a big library no longer freezes the window while you type.
Offline mode: one switch in Settings and Hallucinate makes no internet connections at all. Scrobbles wait and are sent when you turn it off.
"Scrobbling & sharing" in Settings is now "Internet & sharing".
Closing the window asks whether to quit, minimize or keep playing in the tray, and can remember your choice.
The Recap card's glows now follow its rounded corners.
Hallucinate has moved to the Phosphene-dev organisation on GitHub, with a new app ID and website address.
Do more at once, and bring your history with you.

ul.li: Select several songs (Ctrl/Shift+click) and play, queue, rate, like, tag or add them to a playlist together
Undo queue changes with Ctrl+Z
Import play counts, ratings and playlists from Strawberry, Clementine, Rhythmbox, MusicBee and iTunes
Skip tracking, used by smart playlists and radio
Headphone crossfeed, fixable lyrics timing, and every missing cover fetched at once
CUE sheets inside audio files, and waveforms for CUE songs
Searchable settings in sections, a better fit for small and tiled windows, and Copy debug info for bug reports
Pride themes: Pride, Trans (dark and light), Bi, Lesbian, Nonbinary, Pan and Ace, calm and readable, with each flag in the backdrop and a slim stripe under the logo
The welcome's theme picker scrolls and shows each flag
Fixed white, unreadable rows in the Stats page's top artists and albums
The sidebar no longer overlaps itself in short windows (tiling window managers, fractional scaling)
Accent colours taken from dark album covers stay readable

description.p: More ways into your library, and a better fit for your ears.

ul.li: Artist pages with your listening, top songs and the discography by year
Recap: a week, month or year of listening summed up, with a card to save
Folder view, star ratings (usable in smart playlists) and CUE sheet albums played as separate songs
ReplayGain measured for songs without tags, and headphone correction from AutoEQ
Karaoke-style lyrics in Now Playing, and M3U/PLS playlist import and export
A first-run welcome to choose your music, a theme and scrobbling

description.p: A new look and a lot more to explore.

ul.li: A design of its own: glass panels over colours from the playing cover, a floating player and a waveform seek bar
Now Playing with GPU visualizers (Liquid, Aurora, Nebula) and a spinning-record mode
Home about your library: a random album, a listening heatmap, albums to rediscover and "On this day"
Album pages with liner notes, a colour wall and a timeline
A searchable history of every listen
Signal path readout, library health check and a command palette (Ctrl+K)
Radio mode: when the queue runs out, similar songs from your library keep playing
Smart playlists that update automatically from rules
Choose the audio output device; it is remembered and restored when plugged back in
Save the queue as a playlist, and drag files or folders onto the window to play them
Gapless playback: every track now plays to its last sample, with no cut-off or gap between tracks
The last track of a queue also plays to the end
Fixed a freeze when changing track right after seeking
The window and media controls show the Hallucinate icon in Flatpak
Optional format and bitrate badges in song rows and the now-playing bar
Detected codecs are reported separately from file extensions
Spectrum visualizer, drag-reorderable queue, sleep timer and playback speed
ListenBrainz scrobbling and listening-history import
Discord Rich Presence, listening statistics and duplicate detection
Command-line playback controls and desktop notifications
Liked songs and playlists, ReplayGain, crossfade and an equalizer
Tag editor, cover art fetching and synced lyrics
Mini player and system tray icon
Themes and Last.fm scrobbling
